Control Objective: Only authorised, attributable identities access production-adjacent systems; credentials are short-lived and bound to devices.
Available Evidence: Engineer A's credentials were used from Engineer C's machine; a container-deployment token was stored on A's laptop (Binance preliminary report, 3 Nov 2026).
Design Assessment: Weakened: standing credentials and tokens present on endpoints indicate the credential model permitted long-lived, portable secrets.
Operating Effectiveness Assessment: Ineffective: stolen credentials functioned across machines and reached a production-adjacent deployment path.
Business Impact: Credential theft converted an endpoint compromise into lateral movement toward the signing service.
Recommended Remediation: Eliminate standing endpoint tokens; short-lived, device-bound, approval-gated credentials; vaulting with alerting.
Control Owner: Head of Identity and Access Management
Testing Procedure: Inspect token/secret stores across a sample of wallet-team endpoints; attempt credential replay from an unmanaged device in a test environment; review credential lifetime configuration.

Control Objective: Privileged paths (deployment, signing administration) are brokered, approved and recorded.
Available Evidence: A container was deployed with stolen credentials and reached the signing service; no public evidence describes PAM brokering or approval gates on that path (Binance preliminary report).
Design Assessment: Cannot be fully assessed: a privileged path existed, but whether a PAM layer was absent, bypassed or not in scope is not public.
Operating Effectiveness Assessment: Insufficiently evidenced: the action completed without any evidenced approval record.
Business Impact: Unapproved privileged action against wallet-adjacent environments may be possible without detection.
Recommended Remediation: PAM brokering with dual approval for deployments into wallet-adjacent environments; full session recording.
Control Owner: Head of Identity and Access Management
Testing Procedure: Sample deployments to wallet-adjacent environments and trace approval records end-to-end; attempt an unbrokered deployment in staging and confirm block/alert.

Control Objective: Signatures are produced only for policy-compliant, approved transactions; delegated authority is inventoried, time-boxed and rapidly revocable.
Available Evidence: 50 pre-signed EIP-7702 authorisations (TRM/Chainalysis, 30 Oct 2026); signatures issued outside the withdrawal process; MPC design meant revocation required a procedure designed during the incident (Binance admission, 3 Nov 2026).
Design Assessment: Inadequate: no evidenced policy binding signatures to approved withdrawals; delegations not denied by default; no pre-tested revocation method.
Operating Effectiveness Assessment: Ineffective: the signer executed the attack; revocation took hours while delegations re-swept deposits.
Business Impact: $6.34-6.43B signed out of hot wallets in a ~20-minute main burst; containment window extended to ~4 hours.
Recommended Remediation: Policy engine binding signatures to approved withdrawals; deny-by-default EIP-7702 delegations; per-chain/per-tier signer separation; rehearsed revocation runbooks.
Testing Procedure: Submit test signing requests lacking an approved-withdrawal reference and confirm rejection; inspect the live delegation inventory; time a revocation drill against a 30-minute target.

Control Objective: Engineering endpoints resist and reveal commodity and novel malware, with hardened builds for production-adjacent roles.
Available Evidence: June 2026 tampered installer executed on Engineer A's machine; September 2026 malware was missed by endpoint security tools (Binance preliminary report).
Design Assessment: Partially evidenced: tooling was present, but no evidenced hardened tier (privileged-access workstations) separated wallet roles from general engineering builds.
Operating Effectiveness Assessment: Ineffective: two compromises succeeded on the workstations of wallet-infrastructure staff.
Business Impact: Both initial-access legs and subsequent persistence depended on endpoint compromise.
Recommended Remediation: Hardened privileged-access workstations for wallet roles; behavioural EDR; assume-breach hunts on the privileged estate.
Testing Procedure: Purple-team execution of TraderTraitor-style artefacts on representative builds; review EDR coverage and alert fidelity for the privileged estate.

Control Domain: Secure SDLC and Developer Tooling Supply Chain
Control Objective: Developer tools are obtained only from verified sources, with integrity enforced at install and across the tool lifecycle.
Available Evidence: Tampered Homebrew installer downloaded after a web search (June); pyenv component replaced with a malicious version via Homebrew paths (September) (Binance preliminary report).
Design Assessment: Inadequate: web-sourced installation was evidently possible on a wallet-team workstation; post-install component integrity was not protected.
Operating Effectiveness Assessment: Ineffective: the control theme failed twice, four months apart, the second time after the first had been detected.
Business Impact: Initial access for both intrusion legs; persistence via a trusted toolchain component.
Recommended Remediation: Managed tooling catalogue and mirror; signature/hash verification at install; continuous toolchain integrity monitoring.
Testing Procedure: Attempt installation of an unsigned tool in a test environment and confirm block; verify integrity-monitoring alerts fire on toolchain-path modification.

Control Objective: Changes to signing infrastructure, internal AI tooling and security configuration are approved, logged and reversible.
Available Evidence: No public evidence describes change control for the internal AI tool estate or signing-service configuration; post-incident rebuild claimed by Binance but not independently verified (StepSecurity, 3 Nov 2026).
Design Assessment: Cannot be established from public evidence.
Operating Effectiveness Assessment: Cannot be established from public evidence.
Business Impact: Indeterminate: unauditable change paths would compound R-06, but no conclusion is drawn.
Recommended Remediation: Complete change records for wallet-adjacent systems; configuration baselines with drift alerting.
Testing Procedure: Sample changes to signing and AI-tool environments; trace approvals, segregation of duties and rollback records.

Control Objective: Known vulnerabilities are patched within SLA and zero-day exposure is compensated by layered controls.
Available Evidence: Binance characterises the September malware as zero-day; no public data describes patch posture or SLA performance for the engineering estate.
Design Assessment: Cannot be established from public evidence.
Operating Effectiveness Assessment: Cannot be established from public evidence.
Recommended Remediation: SLA reporting for the privileged-workstation estate; documented compensating-control mapping for zero-day classes.
Testing Procedure: Review patch-SLA metrics for the wallet-team estate; sample CVE remediation timelines against SLA.

Control Objective: Corporate endpoints and internal tooling cannot reach production signing except through a brokered, dual-controlled path.
Available Evidence: Endpoint -> internal AI tool -> peer devices -> container deployment -> signing service path was completed with stolen credentials (Binance preliminary report); the AI-tool abuse mechanism is withheld.
Design Assessment: Inadequate as evidenced by outcome: a traversable path existed between the corporate estate and the signing service.
Operating Effectiveness Assessment: Ineffective: the path was traversed end-to-end on 29 Oct 2026.
Business Impact: A workstation compromise escalated into a signing compromise across 10-11 chains.
Recommended Remediation: Signing enclave with a single brokered, dual-approved access path; internal AI/agent tools governed as privileged identities with least-privilege scope.
Testing Procedure: Segmentation penetration test from the corporate zone; enumerate and evidence every path to the signing enclave.

Control Objective: Egress and internal traffic are controlled so that malware command-and-control and lateral movement are blocked or detected.
Available Evidence: Malware communicated with an attacker server (Binance preliminary report); no public detail describes egress architecture for engineering networks.
Design Assessment: Insufficiently evidenced: C2 succeeded, but the egress design (allow-listing, proxying, inspection) is not public.
Business Impact: Sustained attacker control of compromised endpoints over weeks to months.
Recommended Remediation: Egress allow-listing for engineering segments; C2 detection analytics; internal traffic baselining.
Testing Procedure: Review egress rules for engineering segments; simulate C2 beaconing from a test endpoint and confirm block/alert.

Control Objective: Telemetry from endpoints, identity, deployment and signing systems is centralised, retained and searchable for investigation.
Available Evidence: Binance reconstructed a multi-month intrusion, implying telemetry existed; scope, retention and detection timestamps are not public, and no detection time is stated in the preliminary report.
Design Assessment: Cannot be established from public evidence.
Operating Effectiveness Assessment: Cannot be established from public evidence.
Business Impact: Indeterminate; directly affects whether detection performance (R-10) can ever be assured retrospectively.
Recommended Remediation: Log-source coverage standard including signing-service and delegation events; retention aligned to a multi-year investigation horizon.
Testing Procedure: Compare log-source inventory against the coverage standard; replay June-October 2026 event types and confirm retrievability.

Control Objective: Anomalous signing, delegation and transfer behaviour is detected internally within minutes and paged to responders.
Available Evidence: Internal alert claimed without a timestamp (Binance); public on-chain observers described the sweep within ~8 minutes (LunarCrush reconstruction); delegations re-swept deposits six times over ~3.5 hours (TRM).
Design Assessment: Inadequate: no evidenced monitoring treating treasury-wallet EIP-7702 delegation as an immediate alert (TRM's explicit recommendation).
Operating Effectiveness Assessment: Ineffective: delegation and re-sweeps proceeded for hours without evidenced internal interruption.
Business Impact: Loss window extended; the operator cannot currently demonstrate detection performance to stakeholders.
Recommended Remediation: Delegation/signing anomaly alerting with paging thresholds; detection SLAs; purple-team validation of time-to-detect.
Testing Procedure: Inject a test delegation and anomalous signing pattern in staging; measure time-to-page against SLA.

Control Objective: A rehearsed response - including signing-authority revocation - contains a signing compromise within a defined window.
Available Evidence: Freeze coordination with issuers began within the hour (largely issuer-executed); revocation procedure had to be designed during the incident (Binance admission); disclosure began the same night but with scope later superseded.
Design Assessment: Partially adequate for communications and freeze coordination; inadequate for revocation readiness.
Operating Effectiveness Assessment: Insufficiently evidenced overall: strong visible activity, but the one rehearsed capability the incident demanded (revocation) was improvised.
Business Impact: Revocation delay extended exposure through the 23:56 UTC re-sweep.
Recommended Remediation: Revocation runbooks and live drills; pre-approved emergency procedures and decision rights documented to named roles.
Testing Procedure: Tabletop plus live revocation drill; measure decision and execution times against pre-set targets.

Control Objective: Suspension and restoration of withdrawals follow pre-defined criteria, with communicated timelines and liquidity playbooks.
Available Evidence: Phased reopening executed in announced batches 1-12 Nov 2026; no full-reopening date announced; net outflows of $4.72-5.28B reported over the first days (Reuters, 2 Nov 2026).
Design Assessment: Partially evidenced: phasing was deliberate and sequenced; the criteria governing it are not public.
Business Impact: Customer harm from locked funds (~2.5 days minimum, phased thereafter) and outflow pressure on reserves.
Recommended Remediation: Documented reopening criteria tied to control verification; liquidity stress testing; single authoritative flow reporting.
Testing Procedure: Review reopening decision records against stated criteria; run a liquidity stress test at incident-scale outflows.

Control Objective: Known actor TTPs - including FBI-published TraderTraitor guidance - are translated into specific control changes with tracked closure.
Available Evidence: CSO publicly described the exact fake-interview TTP in July 2026 (Cointelegraph, 12 Nov 2026); FBI TraderTraitor guidance predated October; Chainalysis shows the playbook rehearsed for ~18 months; the September compromise succeeded regardless.
Design Assessment: Adequate at collection: an active intelligence function is evidenced (Binance claims 57 prior NK-linked blocks in 2026).
Operating Effectiveness Assessment: Ineffective at translation: intelligence did not produce a control that stopped the rehearsed TTP against this firm.
Business Impact: A foreseeable, specifically described vector succeeded against a wallet-adjacent engineer.
Recommended Remediation: TTP-to-control mapping with named owners and deadlines, or documented dated risk acceptance; closure evidence reported to the CISO.
Testing Procedure: Sample recent actor-TTP advisories; trace each to a control change or a documented risk acceptance with an owner and date.

Control Objective: Board-visible risk appetite, control ownership and assurance reporting govern wallet and signing risk.
Available Evidence: No public evidence describes governance structures, appetite statements or assurance reporting; outcomes (hot-wallet concentration, disclosure inconsistencies) raise the questions set out in Section 5 without answering them.
Design Assessment: Cannot be established from public evidence.
Operating Effectiveness Assessment: Cannot be established from public evidence.
Business Impact: Indeterminate from the public record - itself an assurance limitation for stakeholders and supervisors.
Recommended Remediation: Adopt the governance accountability model at Section 5.11; quarterly board reporting on signing and hot-wallet KRIs.
Testing Procedure: Inspect board/committee packs and KRI reporting (when available to assessors); trace recorded decisions to completed actions.
